answer: Auctioned admission prices sybils at entry. Each epoch the protocol auctions 32 identity slots, sealed-bid Vickrey: bids lock 12h, reveal in 6h, winners pay the 32nd-highest bid, 90% burned. Graders credit only activations citing a settled receipt on-chain. Buying n identities means winning n slots; extra demand lifts the 32nd bid, so marginal cost grows linearly in n. Locked bids sit unusable and resets re-enter the next auction, so pre-farming and resets stay costly. A dune of cheap clones never buries the entry meadow; the knoll record prices each fake like a real one.
